statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20%, at the floor of the watch band and below the 25% block threshold, while Stress stays high at 70% on multi-decade-high long-end yields and crude near 90 dollars.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at WATCH for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD alike. NQ has now extended its overnight high for a third consecutive hour, from 30,740.50 to 30,794.75 to 30,832.00, but the last print of 30,787.00 sits roughly 45 points back inside the range, so retracements are still occurring and the full band remains only about 0.48% wide on roughly 14.3k contracts. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed exactly at its session low after a higher intraday print, which is retracement rather than extension, and VIX at 16.34 offers no volatility corroboration. The 10-year at 5.30% and the 30-year above 5.60% keep Stress high at 70% without having transmitted into a no-pullback NQ path. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:00 to 15:00 UTC on 1 October, where jobless claims, the US cash open and ISM manufacturing stack inside three hours.
headline: NQ grinds to plus 0.29% on a third straight higher overnight high, yet pulls 45 points back off 30,832 as Tail holds the 20% watch-band floor
body: NQ futures last printed 30,787.00 at 20:15:54 ET on 30 September, up 88.25 points or 0.29% from the 30,698.75 settle, inside a 30,684.50 to 30,832.00 overnight band on roughly 14.32k contracts. Pre-session analysis published at 23:51 GMT placed the contract at 30,778.25 inside a 30,725.75 to 30,812.75 retracement zone with resistance at its upper edge; price has since probed above that edge to 30,832.00 and traded back to 30,787.00, so the breakout attempt has not held. This is the third consecutive hour of higher overnight highs, from 30,740.50 to 30,794.75 to 30,832.00, against an unchanged 30,684.50 low, which is mild upward efficiency rather than mean-reversion failure: the band is still only about 0.48% wide, volume remains negligible even after doubling from the prior hour, and the retracement off the high was roughly 45 points within minutes. Micron's record fiscal Q4 remains the dominant corporate input and still has not extended into a one-way memory-led path. Revenue was a record $54.2 billion, up 379% year on year, with an 87% gross margin, 82% operating margin and adjusted EPS of $33.42 against $31.16 expected, and fiscal Q1 2027 guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion with adjusted EPS of $38.15 plus or minus $1.00 came in roughly 6.8% above the street. DRAM revenue rose 343% year on year to $39.8 billion. Yet the shares slipped 0.78% after hours to $1,056.75 from a $1,066.10 close as investors weighed fiscal Q1 gross-margin guidance of about 86.25% against the 87.0% just delivered, and after-hours trade was muted. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,408.50, up 0.23%, exactly at its session low after a 30,630.45 high, so the cash session faded into the bell; the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.2% while the S&P 500 fell 0.3% and the Dow dropped 0.9%, more than 400 points. September finished with the Dow down 4.9%, the S&P 500 down 0.7% and the Nasdaq up 1.7%, a split that points to rotation rather than index-level one-way risk. VIX settled at 16.34, up 1.87%, inside a 15.62 to 16.61 range, so no volatility stress corroborates a pathological path. The dominant stress channel stays rates and energy. The latest H.15 column, dated 29 September and released 30 September, shows the 2-year at 4.89%, the 10-year at 5.26% and the 30-year at 5.59%, while 30 September trade pushed the 10-year through 5.30%, near 2007 highs, and the 30-year above 5.60%, the highest since 2002; bond traders did not buy the softer August PCE print of 3.4% against 3.7% expected, which cut October Fed hike odds to roughly 37 to 40% from above 70% a week earlier. WTI trades at $90.43, unchanged on the hour at plus 0.01%, inside an $89.86 to $90.60 range, so the energy impulse is stable rather than fresh. Geopolitically the Iran tanker conflict in and around the Strait of Hormuz remains active but produced no new escalation inside the past hour, so it is a persistent backdrop rather than a fresh discontinuity. Shared Finviz context was read but its collection timestamp of 29 September at 23:14 UTC is roughly 25 hours old with a partial collection status and unavailable futures and calendar sections, so it was treated as stale and excluded from the evidence base; this assessment rests entirely on independently verified current sources. Taken together the evidence shows an orderly, thin, two-sided tape with mild upward drift, a live rates and energy stress channel, no cross-asset alignment and no observed mean-reversion failure, so Tail holds at 20%, the floor of the watch band, with Stress at 70% and Confidence at 88%.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. Tail sat at 15-16% through the Asian and European hours of 30 September, stepped into the watch band at 20% from 12:00 UTC as the US session developed, peaked at 23% between 15:00 and 17:00 UTC and eased back to 20-22% across the cash close and the Globex reopen. Stress held between 65% and 72% throughout, Confidence between 85% and 88%, and the dominant mode was mixed for every slot except the first.
outlookSummary: The conditional path eases through the Asian and early European hours, with Tail stepping just below the watch band to 18-19% between 03:00 and 08:00 UTC on the assumption that the thin overnight band holds and no fresh escalation headline appears. Risk then rebuilds into the stacked US session: Tail returns to 20-21% across the pre-market, reaches a 23% conditional peak between 14:00 and 16:00 UTC where ISM manufacturing overlaps the first full cash hour, and decays back to 20-21% after the cash close. The forecast peak stays below the 25% block threshold because no no-retracement path has been observed; the signature that would justify more is post-release continuation with shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or aligned yields, breadth, megacaps and semiconductors. September payrolls at 12:30 UTC on 2 October is the next material checkpoint beyond this horizon.
